context.clinical_context_summary: 82-year-old male with significant past medical history of severe sepsis, bacteremia, recurrent UTIs, orthostatic hypotension, benign prostatic hyperplasia with urinary retention, and melena. Currently on midodrine for orthostatic hypotension, dabigatran (anticoagulation), metformin (diabetes), levothyroxine (hypothyroidism), and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (active antibiotic therapy). Presents with general weakness in context of documented fever (mean temp 38.13°C, range 37.7-39.7°C) raising high concern for recurrent sepsis/urosepsis given his history. HIGH RISK PATIENT: History of severe sepsis, on anticoagulation (bleeding risk given melena history), orthostatic hypotension (baseline low BP expected), and elderly with multiple comorbidities. Temperature readings appear consistent with standard oral/core measurement given the elevated values.
context.rationale: Thresholds are adjusted for this high-risk elderly patient with documented orthostatic hypotension on midodrine therapy, explaining his baseline lower systolic BP (mean 94 mmHg); therefore, SBP normal range lowered to 85 mmHg but critical threshold at 75 mmHg given sepsis risk. Heart rate upper limit expanded slightly given age-related variability and potential septic response. SpO2 threshold lowered to 92% as normal minimum given age, but 90% is critical. Temperature normal upper limit set at 38.0°C since he is actively febrile (mean 38.13°C) and any sustained fever >38.5°C warrants escalation given sepsis history. Respiratory rate thresholds account for his current mild tachypnea (mean 21) but rates >28 indicate respiratory decompensation.
